title: UNDERWATER SINCE BIRTH
style:
```
126 BPM, dry close-mic spoken word intro, punchy staccato male vocal,
industrial bass house, sidechained sub-bass, hard-hitting kick drum,
cinematic build, wall of sound anthemic chorus, half-time emotional bridge,
bass-only minimalist outro, dark dystopian electronic, spoken word verses,
tech-noir atmosphere, distorted synth pads, no guitar solos,
human voice raw and unpolished, lyrics-forward mix,
drops that hit like a system crash, builds that feel like trust breaking
```
lyrics:
[Intro — underwater tonal wash, sun frequency rising, slow bass pulse]

  [Verse 1 — sparse, each word deliberate]
  No pool fence back then.
  Hot day. No one watching.
  I walked in.

  Water like air.
  No shock.
  Just in.

  Slow sink to the bottom —
  like a weight that chose to drop.
  Sat on the floor of the pool.
  Looked up.

  Sun getting bigger.
  Brighter.
  Nearly all white.

  I was in bliss.

  Then black.

  [Pre-Chorus]
  Pete's hands.
  On my back.
  Water out.
  Air in.

  [Chorus — full, alive, defiant]
  Underwater since birth — WA kept me
  Pete pulled me up from the bottom, set me free
  Sun was almost white when he got there in time
  That's my brother — been saving me my whole life

  Mum said what the hell are you doing taking off your shirt
  We need to find Corey — he's been gone — he's gone
  Five minutes underwater at the bottom of the deep
  Pete already knew — he's the one I'd keep

  [Verse 2 — tighter, dry, almost amused]
  Doc gave me penicillin.
  Went home skinny.
  Put on weight.
  Look mum — I'm fat now.

  Before I could walk —
  they found me up a tree.
  Needed a climber to get me down.
  That was also me.

  Swan Districts Hospital —
  mum worked there.
  They said sit.
  She said bullshit — I work here.

  Pushed straight through to the doctor.
  Saved me before I died.
  Doc confirmed.
  Thanks mumma.

  [Pre-Chorus]
  Pete's hands.
  Mum's voice.
  No fence.
  No school.
  Bronchitis cleared.
  Still here.

  [Chorus — doubled, full]
  Underwater since birth — WA kept me
  Pete pulled me up from the bottom, set me free
  Mum pushed through the hospital doors — no waiting
  That's the family — never sat still, never debating

  Now Pete skips the Pelican — 62 feet of steel
  The swimmer who held his breath longer than was real
  Malaga yard to Abrolhos reef — same man
  The one who pulled me up is still running the plan

  [Bridge — half-time, bass and one voice, everything else gone]
  I remember the sun.
  Getting bigger.
  Nearly all white.

  I remember bliss.
  Before the black.

  Then Pete's hands.

  That's WA.
  That's family.
  That's the whole story in one pool.

  [Outro — guitar alone, long slow exhale]
  Pete.
  Brother.
  Still here.
  Both of us.
